lesson.menu_desc: Atender o telefone no meio do turno e dizer o que está acontecendo AGORA, sem perder a rotina de vista: present continuous x present simple -- 32 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- Right Now vs Every Day
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Giovanna de Fátima | Lesson 5 -- Right Now vs Every Day
lesson.grammar_point: present continuous for what is happening now, contrasted with present simple for routine

listenings.text: Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. I am sending you a short one, because I am walking to the office right now and my hands are cold. Listen to my site at this moment. The big machine you can hear is cutting the wall, and two engineers are measuring the floor near the ramp. I usually work in the office in the morning, but today is different: I am outside, and I am waiting for a delivery. The truck is late, as always. My boss is having a meeting with the client at the moment, so nobody is answering the phone. Talk to you later.

Good afternoon, everyone. Ray Collins, with a short update for the afternoon shift. Right now the north area is closed, because the crew is moving the big containers. They are working there until four. If you are waiting for a delivery, please hold on: the trucks are coming in through the south gate today, not the main gate. I am taking a look at the schedule for tomorrow, and one thing is already clear: the morning meeting is starting at seven, not at eight. Nobody is late tomorrow, please. Thank you, and stay safe.

extra_audio.text: The phone is ringing, and Giovanna is answering it. She says: Giovanna speaking. Greg is asking what she is doing right now. She says she is measuring the wall, and she asks him to hold on. Finally she takes a look at her notes and gives him the number.
